subject: Data Engineering
title: Continuous Improvement
description: A micro-lesson that makes Continuous Improvement usable.

hook.text: Data quality isn't a project with a finish line. It's a practice that never ends.

buildup.text: New data sources, changing requirements, and team turnover constantly introduce new quality risks.

discovery.text: Regular quality reviews, incident retrospectives, and metric tracking create a feedback loop.

twist.text: The biggest threat to data quality isn't technology — it's complacency after the first win.

climax.text: Teams that treat quality as a culture — not a feature — consistently outperform those that don't.

punchline.text: Quality isn't a destination. It's a daily habit.

quiz.question: Why is data quality a continuous practice rather than a one-time project?
options: New sources and changing requirements constantly introduce new risks
